description:
PROBLEM TYPE: LP

PROBLEM INFO: 

- A manager of an oil refinery has \var{allocated_i} million barrels of crude oil type \var{i} allocated for production during the coming month. 
- These resources can be used to make \var{P} different products. product \var{p} sells for $ \var{price_p} per barrel.
- There are \var{L} production processes. Process \var{l} uses \var{input_l_i} barrels of each crude \var{i}, and produces \var{output_l_p} barrels of each product \var{p}. 
- Process \var{l} has a cost of \var{cost_l} per barrel of product produced.
- All \var{input_l_i} quantities and \var{output_l_p} quanitites are in barrels. 
- There are no separate cost items for the cost of the crudes, as they have already been allocated.

INPUT FORMAT: 

{
    "allocated": [allocated_i for i in 1, ..., O],
    "price": [price_p for p in 1, ..., P],
    "input": [[input_l_i for i in 1, ..., O] for l in 1, ..., L],
    "output": [[output_l_p for p in 1, ..., P] for l in 1, ..., L],
    "cost": [cost_l for l in 1, ..., L]
}

OBJECTIVE: We want to know how many times should we execute each process to maximize the profit for the next month (you can assume that the number of times that each process is executed is a floating point number)

OUTPUT INFO:

- \var{profit} is the total profit for the month.
- \var{execute_l} is the number of times that process \var{l} should be executed.

OUTPUT FORMAT:

{
    "profit": profit,
    "execute": [execute_l for l in 1, ..., L]
}

Input.definition: Input resources required for each option in each process

Output.definition: Output produced for each price point in each process

objective.description: "The goal is to maximize the total profit for the next month by determining how many times to execute each production process."

constraints.description: For each crude oil type i, the total amount used across all processes cannot exceed the allocated amount: sum over l of (input_l_i * execute_l) <= allocated_i
For each process l, the number of times it is executed must be non-negative: execute_l >= 0
